summary: Private inference clouds (Fireworks, Base10, Modal) are growing nearly as fast as frontier labs with very little cash burn — extraordinary business models
summary_extended: Baker argues that private inference cloud companies — specifically Fireworks, Base10, and Modal — represent extraordinary business models, growing nearly as fast as frontier AI labs in their early days while burning very little cash, producing Rule of 40 metrics he describes as 'crazy numbers.' The core product innovation he highlights is Fireworks' 'Nexus,' which allows customers to route queries between their own RL-fine-tuned open-source models and frontier models like Claude and Grok in just three lines of code, achieving better outcomes at roughly half the cost of using frontier models exclusively. Baker sees this as the definitive solution for AI-native companies, evidenced by adoption from Harvey, Cursor, Legora, and others. The investment implication is primarily relevant to private markets — these companies are not publicly listed — though the thesis implicitly suggests competitive pressure on frontier model providers who charge premium inference prices. No publicly traded equities are directly implicated as subjects or clear beneficiaries of this specific thesis.
